thread:
Connor O'Brien: Heads up: we need to lock a release train plan for bundling the Private Observability Minimum Pack into the Private installer. Specifically:
- which installer version gets it by default
- backport policy (existing Private customers)
- customer comms timing / enablement

Looking for owners to confirm by EOW so Release can reserve a slot.

Talia Benson: +1. We’re trying to avoid a repeat of “docs say it’s there but it isn’t” :grimacing:

Bruno Silva: From installer side, we can wire it in behind a feature flag for 1-2 releases if we want a soft launch.
Current branch situation:
- private-installer 1.18.x is what most on-prem customers are pinned to
- 1.19.0 is next “feature” release (tentative mid-March)
- 1.19.x will be our main forward line

Vivek Kulkarni: Product preference: GA the min pack as “supported baseline” as soon as it’s stable, but also need a clear statement for existing customers.
We have at least 3 prospects asking “is this included in Private” in March.

Sean Gallagher: SRE POV: don’t default-enable until we’ve run burn-rate rules in staging under load for ~1 week and tuned noise. If we default-enable too early, support/paging gets hammered and customers will just disable everything.

Allison Grant: Agree. Also the metrics contract changes need to be in place first or dashboards will half-work and we’ll get “pack is broken” tickets.

Connor O'Brien: OK. Proposal for discussion:
1) private-installer 1.19.0 includes the pack bits (charts/configs + validation cmd), but OFF by default unless `--enable-observability-pack` or values.yaml toggles.
2) private-installer 1.19.1 (or 1.20.0) flips default ON for new installs only.
3) backport: only critical fixes to 1.18.x; no new feature default flips.

Does that align?

Markus Klein: From the field: most customers won’t pass flags unless we tell them explicitly. For pilots, we can add it to the runbooks.
But if it’s OFF by default for too long, we don’t get real-world feedback.

Dev Patel: Support asks that when it’s OFF by default, docs must be explicit (“optional/preview”) and we need an escalation path if validation fails.
Also: we need a compatibility matrix callout (installer version x pack version).

Kira Thompson: For comms timing: if 1.19.0 ships with it behind a flag, we can publish docs as “Preview / opt-in” and include a “How to enable” section.
Then GA docs update when default flips.

Sahana Iyer: CI/validation status: we can gate 1.19.0 on promtool + grafana provisioning smoke tests, but we’ll need a stable artifact versioning scheme (pack bundle version pinned in installer).

Bruno Silva: Re backporting: wiring the whole “download/apply/provision” flow into 1.18.x is non-trivial. 1.18.x branch is kind of brittle.
If we commit to backporting, scope it to:
- security patches
- critical bugfixes in the validation command maybe
But not the full packaging mechanism.

Priya Natarajan: +1 to being conservative on 1.18.x. We can provide a manual install path for 1.18.x customers as interim (helm chart + docs), but the “bundled in installer” story should target 1.19+.

Connor O'Brien: Let’s get concrete on dates.
- target cut for 1.19.0: Mar 12 (code freeze Mar 6)
- could do 1.19.1: Mar 26

If default-on needs a week of staging, that pushes default-on to 1.19.1 earliest.

Sean Gallagher: That’s fine if we treat 1.19.0 as opt-in preview.
But for default-on, I want:
- alert noise review signoff
- runbooks linked from alert annotations
- “missing signals” alert group present so we don’t get silent failures

Allison Grant: Also need an explicit “supported signals” checklist output (installer post-install report) so Solutions can validate quickly.

Bruno Silva: That’s already in my queue. We can include a `private-installer validate observability` command in 1.19.0 (preview) and improve output formatting by 1.19.1.

Talia Benson: What do we tell customers?
We need a short statement for TAMs + Sales:
- preview in 1.19.0
- GA default-on in 1.19.1
- existing customers on 1.18.x can opt into manual install or upgrade

Dev Patel: Please add guidance on “upgrade path”: upgrading to 1.19.x doesn’t automatically turn it on unless they enable it (at least in 1.19.0).
We’ve had issues where customers assume new dashboards appear automatically.

Kira Thompson: I’ll draft a “Release notes + enablement” page with those bullets. Need final naming: are we calling it “Private Observability Minimum Pack” or “Observability Pack (Min)” everywhere?

Vivek Kulkarni: Use “Private Observability Minimum Pack” in customer-facing comms. Internally can shorten to “min pack”.

Connor O'Brien: Backport policy draft (please react / comment):
- Installer 1.18.x: no new feature enablement; only critical hotfixes (security + P0 installer bugs). No commitment to bundle the pack.
- Installer 1.19.x: supported line for the min pack.
- Pack artifacts: versioned independently, but installer pins a default pack version; customers can override with `--observability-pack-version` (or local bundle path for airgap).

:thumbsup: = agree
:thinking_face: = concerns

Sean Gallagher added :thumbsup:

Allison Grant added :thumbsup:

Bruno Silva added :thumbsup:

Markus Klein: :thinking_face: on “no commitment to bundle the pack” for 1.18.x. We have at least 2 on-prem customers who won’t upgrade for months.
If we say “upgrade required,” they’ll push back.
Could we do a supported manual install path for 1.18.x and document it as supported-but-not-bundled?

Priya Natarajan: That’s reasonable. “Supported” doesn’t have to mean “bundled,” but we must be clear what Support will help with.

Dev Patel: +1 but we need a firm line: Support can assist if they follow the documented manual steps and pass validation.
If they’ve customized Prometheus/Grafana heavily, it becomes best-effort.

Connor O'Brien: Great. Updating policy wording:
- 1.18.x: supported manual install path (doc + scripts/helm), but bundling into installer is 1.19+ only.

Bruno Silva: For 1.18 manual path: we can ship a tarball of the dashboards/rules/log configs + a helm values snippet.
But we should avoid backporting the “download from control plane” mechanism.

Sahana Iyer: Flagging: if we support manual install, we should still include a promtool validation + a simple “dashboard provisioning check” script so Solutions can verify.
Otherwise we’ll be debugging YAML indentation over Zoom.

Talia Benson: OK, comms plan suggestion:
- Mar 12: 1.19.0 release notes mention preview + opt-in.
- Mar 13-14: send internal enablement note (Sales/TAM/Support) with talk track + who to contact.
- Mar 18: outbound note to active Private customers via TAMs (not broad email) offering opt-in.
- Mar 26: 1.19.1 release notes: GA + default-on for new installs.

Vivek Kulkarni: Works. For prospects in March, we can say “available in preview now; GA end of March.”

Kira Thompson: I’ll need screenshots for the docs (Grafana folder + 1-2 key dashboards) once it’s stable in staging.

Connor O'Brien: Action items:
- Bruno: confirm flag name + config surface (installer flag + helm values) by Monday.
- Sean/Allison: define “default-on readiness” checklist + signoff criteria.
- Kira/Talia: draft comms + release notes language (preview vs GA) + naming consistency.
- Sahana: CI gate list for 1.19.0 (promtool, grafana provisioning smoke, validation cmd).

I’ll add this into the 1.19.0 release train doc and call it out in Wednesday’s release sync.

Redwood Deploy Bot: Reminder: private-installer 1.19.0 code freeze scheduled for 2024-03-06 18:00 PT. Please merge release-blocking PRs before freeze. (reactions: :hourglass_flowing_sand: 3)

Bruno Silva: One more thing: backport cadence. If we find a pack bug after 1.19.0, do we ship a 1.19.0+pack bump without an installer patch?

Connor O'Brien: If the bug is in dashboards/rules only, we can allow “pack-only” patch releases (e.g., pack v0.3.1) and let customers override pack version. But default pinned version in installer only updates with installer patch (1.19.1 etc). That keeps releases predictable.

Sean Gallagher: +1. And for alert rules changes, we should treat it like config changes: need CHANGELOG and call out expected behavior changes (pages less/more).

Dev Patel: Please ensure release notes include “what changed” for alerts. Support gets hammered when pages “disappear” even if it’s intended.

Talia Benson: Noted. I’ll add a section in release notes template: “Alerting changes” + “Dashboard changes”.

Connor O'Brien: Cool. Closing the loop here. Unless there are blockers, we’ll proceed with:
- 1.19.0: min pack preview (opt-in)
- 1.19.1: min pack GA (default-on for new installs)
- 1.18.x: supported manual install path only; critical hotfixes only

Ping this thread if anything changes on the engineering side that impacts these dates.
